Game Mode runtime vs zh-Hans listing copy — two different jobs

Teams assume iOS Game Mode behavior covers storefront language. System Game Mode and App Store Connect actually separate runtime performance from product-page copy:

  • iOS Game Mode on device — system feature that activates when a game is in the foreground: minimizes background activity, reduces Bluetooth latency for controllers, and helps keep frame rate stable. Controls runtime performance — not App Store language. AppLocale does not toggle Game Mode on a device.
  • GameController & Metal frame pacing — wiring controller input, latency tuning, and render-loop optimization in Swift or Objective-C. Listing copy may mention controller latency frames; building Game Mode–aware code is engineering work, not Connect metadata.
  • Background activity throttling during gaming — system dims or defers non-game background work while Game Mode is active. Listing copy describes buyer-visible background-activity dimming badges — not BGTaskScheduler engineering.
  • Gaming session HUD overlays — in-app or system UI that shows Game Mode status, session timer, or performance indicators during play. Listing rewrite covers screenshot caption lines — not HUD implementation in the binary.
  • In-app Game Mode labels — runtime strings on settings toggles, controller pairing sheets, or session banners inside the app. Listing rewrite does not cover String Catalog entries rendered after install.
  • Pricing and Availability → China — makes the app downloadable on the China App Store. Separate from language rows.
  • App Store tab → Chinese (Simplified) localization — independent row for title, subtitle, keywords, description, promotional text, screenshots, and caption lines. Empty or English here means China buyers see English fallback regardless of Game Mode support in the binary.

A game that benefits from iOS Game Mode and a localized China listing are both required when you sell on the China storefront — neither replaces the other.
